package_info.package_versions: Unknown (all versions integrated at time of attack)
package_info.why_malicious: The Picreel marketing script was compromised in a supply chain attack, resulting in the injection of MageCart web skimming code into websites that included Picreel, such as Forbes. The injected code steals payment data from site visitors, making the entire package malicious during the period of compromise.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user submits a checkout or subscription form on a website embedding the compromised Picreel script.
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the main Picreel JavaScript file served to client browsers from Picreel's CDN or vendor infrastructure.
required_permissions: Access to the DOM to read form data
Ability to initiate outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches an event listener to all form submissions, reads all data from the submitted form (including payment and personal information), and sends this data via an HTTP POST request to a hardcoded external attacker-controlled domain, resulting in the exfiltration of sensitive user data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts all form submissions and exfiltrates the complete form data, including sensitive payment and personal information, to an external domain not affiliated with the website. This is a hallmark of web skimming attacks and is not consistent with the expected behavior of marketing scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate marketing scripts should not access or transmit full payment or personal data from checkout forms. They may collect anonymized analytics, but should never exfiltrate sensitive user data to untrusted domains without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors may collect form data, but only to their own secure, vetted endpoints and typically with clear user consent and compliance with security standards such as PCI DSS.
key_indicators: Global event listener attached to form submission events
Reads all fields from submitted forms, including payment details
Sends collected form data to an external, hardcoded, non-affiliated domain
No user notification or consent for data exfiltration
Injected into a third-party marketing script not intended for payment processing

attack_chain.action: MageCart group compromises Picreel's JavaScript supply chain and injects malicious skimming code into the script distributed by Picreel.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to all websites embedding Picreel's script.

attack_chain.action: Victim websites (e.g., Forbes) load the compromised Picreel script from the vendor's CDN, which executes in visitors' browsers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code runs in the context of the victim website, gaining access to the DOM and user interactions.

attack_chain.action: Injected MageCart code hooks into payment or checkout form submissions, collects sensitive data, and exfiltrates it to attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and personal data from site visitors.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that attaches global event listeners to form submission events, especially on checkout or payment forms
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing full form or payment data to domains not affiliated with the website or its payment processor
Unexpected or unauthorized modification of third-party marketing scripts, such as Picreel
file_indicators: Unexpected changes or additions in third-party JavaScript files (e.g., Picreel) loaded from CDN or vendor, such as new event listeners or network requests
Presence of event listeners on sensitive forms (checkout, payment) that are not present in the original, legitimate script
Absence of subresource integrity (SRI) checks or hash mismatches for third-party scripts
network_indicators: Outbound POST requests from client browsers to domains not affiliated with the website or known payment processors (e.g., 'https://malicious-domain.com/collect')
Connections to domains or IP addresses previously associated with MageCart or other web skimming infrastructure
Unusual volume or pattern of POST requests containing form data during checkout events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript code that attaches event listeners to payment or checkout forms and sends form data to external domains. Implement content integrity checks (such as subresource integrity or file hash validation) on all third-party scripts. Analyze client-side network traffic for suspicious POST requests containing sensitive data to unknown or untrusted endpoints. Regularly audit third-party scripts for unauthorized modifications, and maintain an allowlist of approved network destinations for sensitive data.
